prompt_text: I was in a car accident in Pleasanton CA. Which lawyer should I hire for my injury case?
answer_verbatim:
I can help you pick the right lawyer — but first a few quick questions that will change what I recommend:

- How serious are your injuries (minor, require ongoing treatment, surgery, permanent disability)?
- When did the accident happen?
- Was fault disputed or do you have clear evidence someone else caused it?
- Is the other driver insured? Have you spoken to an insurance company yet?
- Do you want a local Pleasanton lawyer, or is any Bay Area personal‑injury firm okay?
- Do you prefer a small firm / solo or a larger firm with more resources?

If you prefer, tell me those details and I’ll tailor recommendations. Meanwhile, here’s practical, useful guidance so you can quickly identify and hire the right attorney.

Immediate steps (if you haven’t done them)
- Get medical care and follow doctors’ orders; document everything.
- Preserve evidence: photos of the scene, vehicle damage, your injuries, witness names/contacts.
- Obtain the police report and copy any medical records and bills.
- Don’t give a recorded statement to the other driver’s insurer without an attorney.
- Note deadlines: in California the normal statute of limitations for personal injury is 2 years from the injury; claims against a government entity have much shorter deadlines (often 6 months). Don’t delay contacting counsel.

How to choose the right lawyer
Look for an attorney who:
- Specializes in personal injury and has experience with auto collisions.
- Has handled cases similar to yours (same injury type, liability situation).
- Works on contingency fee (most PI lawyers do) — you pay only if they recover.
- Has trial experience and is willing to go to court if needed (not all cases settle).
- Communicates clearly and responds promptly.
- Has verifiable client results and good reviews/references.
- Is licensed and in good standing with the State Bar of California.

Where to check credentials and reputation
- State Bar of California website (verify license status, any disciplinary record).
- Client reviews on Google, Yelp, Avvo, Martindale‑Hubbell, Super Lawyers listings.
- Local referrals: primary care doctor, other attorneys, friends/family, or the Tri‑Valley Bar Association.

Questions to ask at the initial consultation
- How many car-accident cases like mine have you handled?
- What were the outcomes (settlements/verdict amounts) for comparable cases?
- Do you handle cases on contingency? What is your fee percentage and are costs advanced?
- Who will work on my case day-to-day (you or an associate/paralegal)?
- How often and by what method will I receive updates?
- What is your approach to settlement vs trial?
- What are the likely obstacles in my case and how would you handle them?
- Estimate of timeline and likely range of value for my claim (given the facts).
- Do you have references from past clients I can call?

Typical fee structure and costs to expect
- Contingency fees usually 33% to 40% if the case settles before litigation; sometimes higher if suit is filed or if the case goes to trial.
- You may also be charged costs (filing fees, expert witness fees, medical record retrieval); many firms advance those costs and deduct them from recovery.
- Ask for the fee agreement in writing and any caps on fees or costs.

Red flags to avoid
- Lawyers who pressure you to sign immediately or promise a specific settlement amount.
- Lack of a written fee agreement.
- Very poor communication or evasiveness about experience or outcomes.
- No references, no online presence, or a bad disciplinary record.

Local search tips (Pleasanton / Tri‑Valley area)
- Search: “Pleasanton car accident lawyer,” “Tri‑Valley personal injury attorney,” or “auto accident attorney Alameda County.”
- Use State Bar lawyer search + “personal injury” and then narrow by location.
- Call 3–5 attorneys for free consultations and compare answers, demeanor, and fees.

If you want, I can:
- Help you draft a short email or phone script to contact attorneys for consultations.
- Create a checklist of documents to bring to consultations.
- Help evaluate 2–3 specific attorneys you find (if you paste their names and any details).

Tell me the accident details and whether you want me to draft a call/email script or a checklist — I’ll prepare that next.
